title: Hybrid Dual-Clock Geo-RoPE Mathematical Prototype and Numerical Simulation
hypothesis: Nesting a 32-D fast token/step RoPE clock inside a 32-D Caelus geocentric physical torus (GAST/ASC, solar altitude, planetary-hour photoperiod phase, Moon longitude, Sun-Moon elongation, solar seasonal longitude) preserves 100% intra-turn token ordering where Caelus-Pure-Geo collapses, preserves post-sleep/post-compaction elapsed ordering where Standard-RoPE collapses, beats fixed-period Unix-Linear-Fourier on high-latitude seasonal photoperiod recurrence (Oslo Dec vs Sept), and eliminates 7d/14d/21d/28d weekly aliasing across 30-day same-clock memory streams.
null_baseline: Standard-RoPE (token index only), Unix-Linear-Fourier (synthetic fixed-period 24h/7d/365.25d UTC sinusoids), and steelman Hybrid-Unix-Fourier (32-D fast token RoPE + 32-D fixed-period 24h/7d/365.25d UTC sinusoids).
success_bar: Hybrid-Dual-Geo-RoPE achieves AUC >= 0.99 on Probe A (confirming Caelus-Pure-Geo collapses near 0.50), AUC >= 0.99 on Probe B (confirming Standard-RoPE collapses near 0.50), beats Unix-Linear-Fourier and Hybrid-Unix-Fourier by >= +0.30 Top-1 accuracy on Probe C Oslo photoperiod recurrence, and achieves lower multi-week collision rate than Unix-Linear-Fourier on Probe D while honestly reporting all probes where Unix-Fourier ties.
kill_criterion: Hybrid-Dual-Geo-RoPE fails to beat Unix-Linear-Fourier / Hybrid-Unix-Fourier on Probe C photoperiod recurrence by at least +0.15 Top-1 accuracy, fails to beat Caelus-Pure-Geo on Probe A, or fails to beat Standard-RoPE on Probe B.
